title: Potentiometer Motor Control Breadboard
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Beginning Electronics
description: Control a small DC motor with a three-terminal potentiometer and 2N2222 NPN transistor on a breadboard. Explore a correctly connected flyback diode with slowed transient playback.

learningObjectives: Adjust potentiometer position and relate base current to motor response.
Trace the protected flyback current path when the potentiometer removes base drive.

keyQuestions: Why does the motor speed saturate?
Which direction does flyback current flow?
commonMisconceptions: Motor current passes through the potentiometer.
The diode prevents excessive motor current.
assessmentOpportunities: Record and explain motor response at five potentiometer settings.
Identify the cathode and trace both current loops.

simulationModel.type: Analytic loaded voltage divider and fixed-gain BJT with steady-state motor load; RL flyback transient
assumptions: BJT beta=80, Vbe=0.7 V, Vce(sat)=0.2 V
Motor R=30 Ω, L=50 mH, back EMF=3s V, load current=20+40s mA
Flyback diode drop=0.7 V; playback slowed 1000×
limitations: No switching storage time, diode recovery or parasitics
Speed is an illustrative steady-state percentage, not RPM
